newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bel-20 could beat record, but not many buyers left.
newsitem.headline: Bel-20 could beat record, but not many buyers left.

text.p: The Bel-20 share index could top its 1996 high on Wednesday provided there were no major losses on Wall Street, the dollar slipped no further and bond yields held steady at the currently low rates.

"Also there are not many buyers out there anymore," a trader said. This was evidenced by the fact that volumes were again moderate at best -- Tuesday's tally for total trade in Belgian shares stood at some 1.5 billion Belgian francs.
The Bel-20 ended Tuesday up 7.94 points, or 0.44 percent, at 1,831.63, just short of its all-time high of 1,831.98, helped by the day's fresh falls in capital market interest rates.

The cheaper refinancing rates attracted buyers to banks with Generale Bank adding a notable 1.6 percent at 11,350 francs in trade worth 153.2 million francs, making the share the leader in volume terms.

Runners-up were insurers Royale Belge, up 2.2 percent at 6,500 francs, and AG, up 1.3 percent at 4,560 francs. Insurers traditionally hold large bond portfolios and thus stand to make capital gains when market rates fall.
Some traders said the insurers also rose amid expections the industry wwould undergo more consolidation after French insurers Axa and UAP said they intended to merge.
UAP and Belgian holding company GBL control Royale Belge. Other traders were not so sure of the impact of the French news. GBL was up just 15 francs at 3,900.
Elsewhere in the financial sector, reshuffling continued ahead of the listing of shares in Gemeentekrediet/Credit Communal, dealers said.

The initial public offering closed on Tuesday, a day early because of heavy demand. On November 20 Gemeentekrediet is due to fix the issue price and trade in the shares, under the name DEXIA CC, to start on the Brussels Stock Exchange. -- Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6810, Fax +32 2 230 7710
